title: Grace, will, and later TULIP framing
summary: What the Fathers actually say about human will, sin, and grace — and where Augustine’s late teaching breaks from earlier patterns. Read as background to later Reformed TULIP slogans, not as those slogans themselves.

title: Father, Son, and Spirit
summary: How early writers speak of the one God and the Son and Spirit — before later creed shorthand. Prefer the timeline and topical excerpts over slogans.

title: Christology: Word, flesh, two natures
summary: Incarnation, against docetism, passion and resurrection, and early two-natures language — the road toward later definitions without pretending Nicaea/Chalcedon are already in Ignatius.

title: Baptism and new birth
summary: Washing, regeneration, Spirit and baptism — what writers actually tie to the water before later slogan wars.

title: Eucharist and thanksgiving
summary: Thanksgiving, presence language, and assembly practice in the loaded excerpts — honest about how thin some stretches still are.

title: Mary and the virgin birth
summary: Ante-Nicene witness centers on the virgin birth and the Word’s birth. Later Marian titles and dogmas are mostly outside this corpus for now.
backlog_note: Broader Mariology (perpetual virginity debates, Theotokos controversy depth) awaits denser Nicene excerpts.

title: Primacy, bishops, and succession
summary: Apostolic succession, bishops and presbyters, and one-church language. Explicit later papal-primacy debates are thin here — do not invent Rome-vs-East excerpts we do not have.
backlog_note: Papal primacy as a dedicated path needs stronger Roman / Petrine controversy coverage.

title: Idols, images, and iconoclasm
summary: Ante-Nicene polemic against idols is live. Eighth-century iconoclasm proper is not yet in this library — stubbed so the question is not forgotten.
backlog_note: True iconoclasm path needs 7th–9th c. witnesses; do not equate Justin’s idol critique with Byzantine icon debates.

title: Pelagian controversy map
summary: Guided path through opposing voices on will, guilt, and grace — Julian’s surviving arguments beside Augustine contrast cards and earlier ante-Nicene patterns.

title: Docetic / phantasm Christ
summary: Writers who refuse a phantasm Christ and insist on real flesh — the early fight that later christological controversies still presuppose.

title: Arian controversy
summary: Father–Son language and one-God claims are present; a full Arian path (Arius, Alexander, Athanasius treatises) is not yet loaded as guided opposing stances.
backlog_note: Add Athanasius / Arius stance pairs when English treatises land.

title: Nestorian / two-natures fights
summary: Cyril’s true-faith works and incarnation/two-natures seeds are in the library. A full opposing-path map (Nestorius vs Cyril with stance tags) is still thin.
backlog_note: Stance-tag Nestorius contrast cards and denser Cyril christology excerpts.

title: Scripture → Fathers
summary: Find who cites a passage across centuries. Use Works find for a verse or book name; Explore hermeneutics and canon topics for how they read Scripture.
backlog_note: Dedicated verse index once scripture tags are uniform across the corpus.

title: Author era bands
summary: Apostolic → ante-Nicene → Nicene → post-Nicene. Same bands drive Works chronology and Explore era filters.

title: First appearance / rupture moments
summary: Where a claim shows up suddenly against long continuity — especially Augustine on will, guilt, and grace beside earlier capable-will patterns.

title: Short reading path for newcomers
summary: A short sequence: one early topic map stop, one whole treatise, one Explore timeline, one later contrast.

title: Original English Translation sampler
summary: Treatises with no previous English translation — filter Works to that set and start with a short Origen text.
